$description: Per-component rules extracted from the spec (design-system.md + components/*.md). Each rule cites its spec section.

global.text: Only use semantic tokens (background-*, object-*, border-*); never hardcode hex, never create color primitives with built-in alpha.
Don't use a background token to color text or vice versa — each token has its own scope (background, text, border, gap, radius).
A component doesn't know which brand it is in; switch brand with data-theme on the container, don't edit the component.
Don't use accent for things you can press: interactive for buttons, links, tabs, field focus, selected items; accent for content emphasis.
background-{status} only pairs with object-on-{status}; object-{status} is for text/icons on light backgrounds.
Don't use negative for a "new" badge, don't use attention for error messages; attention = new and unseen, warning = risk, negative = broken/wrong.
Don't use object-warning (1.92 on white) or object-attention for standalone text — only for dots / icons next to object-primary text.
Don't let color be the only signal where it matters — add text or an icon.
Hover/Pressed only through a full-cover ::after state layer, fill = currentColor (the variant's object color); no background, text or font-weight change.

State-layer opacity steps depend on the background type, not the text color: solid colored backgrounds (Solid Accent / Neutral) → 20/40; light or transparent backgrounds (Outline, Ghost, Solid Inverted) → 5/10; Outline / Ghost Inverted on dark backgrounds → 20/40. Radio is the exception (§6.3d). Disabled and Loading have no state layer.
The Active text mode (one weight step bolder) is only for ToggleButton Active=True and the selected Segment item; it has nothing to do with :hover/:active or State=Pressed.
Don't hardcode width on hugging components (button, toggle, chip); line-height is an absolute value, not a multiplier.
Components read density variables (--control-height-*, --field-height, --text-<style>-*); never hardcode 24/32/40/48/56px, never read --font-size-* directly. Don't use Compact on touch screens.
Only use UU icon (or the set attached via DNA); don't swap in Lucide/Phosphor/Font Awesome singles, don't crop the viewBox. On state uses the fill variant, off state uses outline.
Only build components listed in section 5; anything missing is not decided — ask, don't guess.

TextButtonAccent.text: For the main action of the screen.
One Solid button (Accent or Danger) per screen.
Actions repeated per row or per card are never Solid — use Ghost Small or group them in a "⋯" menu.
Inverted=True when placed on a dark background.
min-width = min-height = the size's height (56/48/32) — a short-label button is never narrower than a circle.
The Outline border does not add to the height: build it with an inset 2px box-shadow, not a border.
Loading: the .loading spinner sits before the label, the label stays visible, no state layer.
Pressed keeps weight 600 — don't use the Active text mode.

TextButtonNeutral.text: Reversible actions (sign out, skip) stay Neutral even if they "look dangerous".
Inverted=True when placed on a dark background.
The Outline border does not add to the height: build it with an inset 2px box-shadow.
Disabled: Solid uses background-disabled, Outline uses border-muted, text object-disabled, no state layer.
Ghost Small is the Action button inside TextInput's suffix and the Huỷ button of SearchInput.
`Type=Tonal` for repeated actions on cards with `background-surface`. Don't place it on `background-subtle`.

TextButtonDanger.text: Only for destructive, irreversible actions (delete account, cancel order, remove device).
Don't use Danger just because a button "looks dangerous" — reversible actions are Neutral.
No Inverted=True — destructive buttons always sit on light backgrounds; on dark screens open a confirmation Dialog.
Per-row destructive actions live in the "⋯" menu and are confirmed by a Dialog with a Solid TextButtonDanger.
One Solid button (Accent or Danger) per screen.
Geometry, density, state layer, Loading and Disabled are identical to TextButtonAccent; only the color family changes to negative.

IconButtonAccent.text: Props and colors match TextButtonAccent (Type/Inverted/Size/State); the icon uses object-* tokens like a Text button's label.
Inverted=True: Solid (surface background) uses state layer 5/10; Outline and Ghost use 20/40.
Icon-only buttons need a name: a label, or a Tooltip with relation='label' (aria-labelledby).
NavigationBar's sub action is IconButtonAccent Solid Inverted=True Base.

IconButtonNeutral.text: Props and colors match TextButtonNeutral; Solid Inverted=False uses background-inverted.
Inverted=True: Solid (surface background) uses state layer 5/10; Outline and Ghost use 20/40.
Icon-only buttons need a name: a label, or a Tooltip with relation='label' (aria-labelledby).
Ghost Small opens the "⋯" Menu for per-row / per-card actions.
The close button (xmark) of Toast, SideSheet and Popover is IconButtonNeutral Ghost; of CardSheet/CardDialog it is Outline Small.
The close button over CardDialog's banner image uses Solid so it reads on any image.
There is no Danger IconButton — per-row delete lives in the "⋯" menu, confirmed by a Dialog with a Solid TextButtonDanger.

ToggleButton.text: For buttons that hold an on/off state; Active is a prop independent of State.
Two separate text props (Label / Active label) to change copy by state — don't share one string.
The icon switches fully between outline ↔ fill when on, not just its color.
Text gets one weight step bolder when on via the Active typography mode, not a weight override on the node.
Don't hardcode width — the two states differ by 1px.
No border, no shadow in any variant — used floating over images or colored backgrounds.
No Loading state; Disabled has no state layer.

ButtonGroup.text: Horizontal: secondary button (Outline) on the left, primary (Solid) on the right, equal widths.
Vertical: primary (Solid) on top, secondary (Outline) below.
Buttons are TextButtonAccent size Large (56), gap 12.
In code, the two equal buttons use flex: 1 1 0, not flex: 1 1 auto.
The shared button group of CardSheet and CardDialog — don't build your own button frame.
Tone=Danger (delete-confirmation dialog / sheet): the primary is TextButtonDanger Solid Large, the secondary stays the same; don't arrange the two buttons yourself.

TextInput.text: Error=True changes three things: border-negative border, Label object-negative, and an Error message caption line under the Field.
The error line is text only, no icon (a fourth signal adds no information).
The error line takes real space (root 76 → 100) — the layout must make room, never overlap other blocks.
Filled + Disabled keeps object-primary text so it stays readable; only the placeholder drops to object-disabled.
Focus/Typing: border-emphasized border + a 1.5×24 object-accent caret.
Report errors at the field with a red border + error line, not a Toast.

TextArea.text: A separate component for multi-line input — replaces any stretched TextInput.
Field height 112 (exactly three lines + counter) — don't change it to 88 or 120; Compact only changes radius and horizontal padding.
Text sticks to the top edge, padding 12 on all sides; the counter (n/100) is caption object-secondary at the bottom right.
Border, background, text and Error follow the TextInput table; the error line has no icon.
Disabled: typed text stays object-primary; label, counter and placeholder drop to object-disabled.

OTPInput.text: Replace every hand-built verification-code field with this component; Masked=True for PINs.
Empty cells show a "-" in object-secondary, not a blank cell or a digit placeholder.
A 2px object-accent caret is the only signal for the cell receiving input.
Error: all six cells get the border-negative border together, no single cell highlighted; background and text unchanged.
Typed digits stay on error — don't clear them.
The error line is centered under the cells, 4 below, caption object-negative.
Never report a wrong code with a Toast.
Cells shrink with flex: 1 0 0, min-width 36, max-width 48 so they don't overflow on narrow phones.

SearchInput.text: No Error — "no results" belongs to the results screen, not the field.
Fixed 24 magnifier icon on the left; the 16 circle-xmark clear button only shows when Filled, 32×32 touch area.
Disabled with text keeps object-primary; the magnifier icon drops to object-disabled.
Loading: a 16 .loading replaces the clear button, border as in Typing.
Cancel=true (a Huỷ button, TextButtonNeutral Ghost Small) only on a dedicated mobile search screen; pressing Huỷ clears text, blurs and closes the panel.
The suggestion / history panel is a Menu Platform=Panel anchored 4 below the field; empty + focus → history, typing → suggestions, nothing → no panel.
"Tìm gần đây" rows end with an IconButtonNeutral Ghost Small xmark to remove each item; the panel stays open, focus returns to the field.
No separate small size — Compact density already shrinks the field.

DateInput.text: Don't combine a TextInput with a calendar icon yourself — use DateInput.
The field takes no typing: tapping opens the OS date picker, no caret, no keyboard.
Value shown as DD/MM/YYYY, body 400 style.
The 24 calendar-days icon is always object-secondary — don't color it object-interactive, don't wrap it in an Icon button; don't swap it for the calendar icon.
Error: border-negative border, Label object-negative, text-only error line.

Dropdown.text: The selected value uses label 600; the empty hint "Bấm để chọn" is body 400 object-secondary.
The 16 chevron-down icon is object-secondary in every state.
No Focus/Typing — the field takes no typing.
Error: border-negative border, Label object-negative, text-only error line.

Menu.text: The option panel of Dropdown, Chip Dropdown and SearchInput suggestions; Platform=Panel on desktop, Sheet on mobile.
Selected row (Single): background-accent-subtle tint, object-interactive text, state layer background-interactive 5/10.
Type=Multiple: Checkbox at the start of the row, no background tint, object-primary text; doesn't close on select, turns on the "Bỏ chọn" + "Áp dụng" Footer.
Turn on Search (unlabeled SearchInput, sticky on top) when > 8 options; no options left → "Không tìm thấy "{từ khoá}"".
.MenuSection: title-xs object-secondary UPPERCASE; .MenuDivider 1px border-muted, the first group needs no line above.
Panel anchored 4 below the element; flips up when there is no room; max height 320, then scrolls inside the panel (quick search sticky on top, footer sticky at the bottom).
Closes on selection (Single), outside click, Esc; Multiple only applies on "Áp dụng".
Options needing more explanation → a Description caption object-secondary under the name, max 2 lines; icon / checkbox top-aligned.
"Chọn tất cả" (Multiple, from 4 options): first row + MenuDivider; Checked when all are selected, Indeterminate when some; while quick-searching it only affects visible options.

Checkbox.text: Checked is a solid background-interactive block + a 20 check fill icon in object-on-interactive.
Indeterminate is a rounded 16×2 bar — not a font minus or a minus icon; pressing it goes to Checked.
Indeterminate is for a "select all" box when the list is partly ticked.
Error when a required box is unticked and the user pressed continue (e.g. agreeing to the Terms).
Never report a checkbox error with a Toast — report it at the box with an object-negative text line under the row.
The 2px border is built inside (inset box-shadow); the state layer covers the border too.

CheckboxInput.text: The touch area is the whole row, not just the box.
Box + text gap 12, top-aligned (items-start), text wrapper padded 4 on top.
The text is the Label property (TEXT), overridden on the instance.

Radio.text: Pick one of many in a form.
32 circle; when selected it stays white with a border-interactive border + a 20 object-interactive dot.
Error when a required radio group has no selection or an invalid one.

RadioInput.text: The touch area is the whole row, not just the 32 circle.
Top-aligned (items-start), gap 12, text block padded 4 on top — not centered.
Lists: a 6/6 dashed border-muted line between rows, none after the last; built with a repeating gradient, not a dashed border.

Switch.text: Toggles a setting that takes effect immediately — unlike Checkbox (select, then confirm).
The knob changes both position and size (16 → 28 with a check fill) — don't just slide a same-size knob.
Off half uses state layer 5/10, on half 20/40; built with currentColor.
A switch with a label is a row: use ListItem with a Trailing Switch (§6.32), don't build the row yourself.
No separate small size (use Compact) and no On/Off text in the track.

Chip.text: A pressable label that holds a selected state; used for filtering (identical cards, just fewer).
Geometry copies TextButtonNeutral Small; text uses the label style.
Selected: background-interactive-muted background, border-interactive border, object-interactive text.
Don't use background-emphasized as the selected chip background — it equals background-disabled.
Selected Type=Select has a 16 check fill icon before the text — never rely on color alone.
Type=Dropdown has a 16 chevron-down in the text color, no check icon; when open the chip is Selected=True with chevron-up.
The panel that opens is a Menu: single-value filter → Single, closes on select; multi-value filter → Multiple + footer, label "{Tên} · n".
16 prefix icon in the text color, gap 8; selected Type=Select puts the check in its place — a chip has only one leading icon.
Type=Input: unselected colors, a 16 xmark in a 24 circle at the end is the only remove button (aria-label "Gỡ {nhãn}"); the chip body is not pressable.
Type=Input for entered values / applied filters; after removal focus moves to the next chip.
No size other than 32 — Compact uses 24.

SegmentedControl.text: Pick one of many as pill tabs when the same content only changes its view.
The selected item gets bolder via the Active mode (.uu-is-active), no weight override.
Item state layer uses an object-primary fill at 5/10 for both Active values.
Items HUG — don't split the width equally unless the screen requires it, don't hardcode 204.
Shell background-emphasized; the selected item has background-surface + elevation-low.

NavigationBar.text: No background of its own — transparent, sitting on the screen background.
Back is IconButtonNeutral Solid Inverted=True Base with chevron-left.
Turn off .Mini App Control with the Mini app prop when the screen doesn't run in a mini app.
A frosted-glass bar is a product choice; the component never turns it on itself.
Use Breadcrumb on desktop; never use Breadcrumb instead of NavigationBar in an app.

BottomBar.text: Navigates between peer main screens; pressing an item changes screen, it doesn't filter content.
The selected item is in the interactive family (not accent), icon outline → fill.
The badge is a NotificationBadge Count anchored to the icon's top right; only on non-Active items.
The standalone action button (FooterItemSpecial) is for one main action, not a navigation destination; Emphasized by default, Subtle when the screen already has a Solid button.
With an action button, Compact=True and at most 4 items.
A frosted-glass bar is not a BottomBar property — the component never turns it on itself.

TablePagination.text: The bar under a table with pressable page numbers — unlike Pagination (carousel indicator bars).
Back on the first page / forward on the last page are Disabled.
≤ 7 pages show all; more than 7 keeps the first, the last, the current ± 1, and gaps become one "…" cell.
Never use "…" in place of exactly one page number.
The Ellipsis cell is not pressable, has no state layer, aria-hidden.
No page-number input to jump — the "…" shortening is enough.

Breadcrumb.text: The location path in the page tree on desktop.
The last item is always the current page: object-primary, not a link, aria-current="page", no Hover.
Never use Breadcrumb instead of NavigationBar in an app.
More than 4 items: keep the first and the last 2; the middle items collapse into one Type=Overflow "…" item that opens a Menu.
No icon before the first item.

SideNav.text: The vertical navigation bar of a web app / portal — the equivalent of BottomBar in an app.
One Active item at a time: background-interactive-muted background, object-interactive fill icon, aria-current="page".
Collapsed: 73 wide, hides labels / chevrons / group titles / level-2 items; labels become Tooltips.
Show/hide labels via the layout collection (data-layout="collapsed" or the collapsed prop), don't create a new collection.
Level=2 items have no icon, indented 24 so their labels align with level-1 labels.
Chevron-down rotates 180° when the group is open (same icon); the item has aria-expanded.
Item badge: a NotificationBadge Count at the end of the item; collapsed it becomes a Dot at the icon's top right.
Collapse / expand button: IconButtonNeutral Ghost Small sidebar-left at the top of the bar, aria-expanded, label "Thu gọn / Mở rộng thanh điều hướng".
No level-3 items — beyond 2 levels, split into pages.

Tab.text: Switches between different content areas (the layout below changes), not for filtering a list.
Active tab: object-interactive text + a 32×4 border-interactive bar fixed at 32, not stretched to the label.
Don't use object-accent for tab text — tabs belong to the interactive family.
Hover/Pressed only on non-Active tabs; Disabled has no state layer.
No shell, background or border of its own on Tab.
16 icon before the text (gap 8) in the text color, fill when Active; a NotificationBadge Dot after the text (gap 4) signals something new.
The badge is only secondary info — the tab label still stands on its own; on the web add hidden text "có mới".

TabBar.text: Fixed for 2–4 short-label tabs (equal widths); Scrollable for ≥ 5 tabs or long labels.
A 1px border-muted bottom border runs the full width; the Active bar sits over it.
Web: role="tablist", left/right arrows switch tabs.
Scrollable: the Active tab scrolls into view automatically.

Pagination.text: A row of bars showing the position in a carousel — not round dots.
Only three positions, Begin/Middle/End, with exactly five bars, even with more than 5 pages.
Width is the main signal (24 vs 16), color only secondary.
Inactive bars use overlay, not a brand background color; 🔒Base/Slick is never used on its own.

Toast.text: Reports the result of what the user just did, at the bottom, with a Type.
Background lightness decides all three elements: Warning (light background) → content, Action button and close button are all Inverted=False; the other three types Inverted=True.
Content uses object-on-{status}; body 400 style, not label.
Never use Toast for flow-blocking errors or input errors (wrong OTP, required checkbox) — Toast disappears by itself.
Errors fixable right away → Dialog / Toast, not an error screen.

Badge.text: A pill-shaped status label, not pressable.
A 16 fill icon always shows before the text, by tone: Neutral circle-info · Success circle-check · Warning circle-warning · Error triangle-warning.
No size other than 24, no Highlight, the icon can't be turned off.

StatusIndicator.text: Container=None: object-{tone} dot, text always object-primary (warning is only the dot).
The dot pulses (opacity 1 → 0.3, 1.6s); it stays still when the user enables reduced motion.
Highlight for "this item deserves attention" (Mới, Nổi bật, Đề xuất), uses the accent family.
Don't use Highlight for errors (Error) or "new and unseen" (NotificationBadge).

CardPushNotification.text: Reports events from outside (order status changes, gifts, messages), slides in from the top; unlike Toast, which reports the result of an action.
No type, no buttons: press the whole card to open, swipe up to dismiss.
Hides itself after 5 seconds, pauses the countdown while touched / hovered.
One card at a time — a new card replaces the old one.
Title and Content max 2 lines; the 48 source image can be hidden.
Desktop: top right corner, 16 from the top and right edges, 360 wide (size-90); pauses the countdown on hover.
No close button, received time or card stacking.

NotificationBadge.text: A dot/count signaling something new and unseen, placed on the corner of an icon or tab.
Uses the attention family — not negative, not warning, not accent.
The attention background is rose-600 (white text 4.70): don't change it to red-600, it would collide with negative.
Don't invent extra variants; the screen positions the anchor.

Tooltip.text: A short label explaining an element on hover or focus — usually for text-less IconButtons or a collapsed SideNav.
Plain text only — no links / buttons inside (use Popover for that).
Shows on hover and on keyboard focus.
Not used on touch screens — there is no hover.
aria-describedby by default; when the tooltip is the name of an icon-only element → aria-labelledby (relation='label').
Hover shows after 500 ms, keyboard focus shows immediately; leaving / blur / Esc hides immediately, no fade.
No multi-line tooltips with titles — use Popover.

TableHeaderCell.text: Numeric columns Align=Right: the sort icon goes before the label, pushed right.
Hover/Pressed only on sortable columns (Sort≠Off); Sort=Off has no icon, no states.
Label object-secondary; object-primary when Ascending / Descending.
Height and padding via density variables (table/header-height, table/cell-padding-x).
Row-selection column: TableHeaderCell Type=Checkbox, 64 wide — Checked when the whole visible page is selected, Indeterminate when some.

TableCell.text: Hover / Selected are states of the whole row — every cell in a row shares the State.
Numeric columns right-align both header and cells, tabular-nums.
Per-row actions are never Solid; two or more actions → one Ghost Small, the rest in the "⋯" menu.
Tables have no outer border, no vertical lines — only a bottom border on each cell.
Tables are for desktop / dashboards (Compact density); Selected uses background-interactive-muted.
An empty table uses EmptySection inside the table body.
Status columns use TableCell Type=Status containing a StatusIndicator; don't put an indicator in a Text cell yourself.

KPICard.text: A card with one main number on a dashboard.
Polarity=Normal: Up object-positive, Down object-negative (color follows the number's direction).
Metrics where up is bad (costs, cancellation rate) → Polarity=Inverse: Up colored negative, Down positive; the icon still follows the direction.
Value heading-base tabular-nums; Trend=[No trend] has no Delta.
Pressable card (Interactive): a 16 chevron-right at the end of the Label row, state layer 5/10 over the whole card; the whole card is one link, no other buttons inside.

CardSheet.text: Back and Close are mutually exclusive: the root sheet is Navigation=Close, a child sheet Navigation=Back (no close button).
Code: passing onBack means Navigation=Back; not passing it means Close.
The button group is ButtonGroup (§6.9), not a hand-built frame; the secondary button and direction are set on the ButtonGroup instance.
All four corners radius 24 — the sheet floats 12 from the edges.
Title via the Header prop; CTA shows/hides the whole button group.
Draggable sheet: a 32×4 rounded-circle Handle with border background at the top; two stops Height=Fit / Full.
Dragging down from Fit past 1/3 → closes; from Full → back to Fit; without a Handle it can't be dragged.

Sheet.text: A screen template, not a product component — in code rebuild the scrim + wrapper, drop the home indicator.
Scrim overlay (black 10%) + overlay-blur 16; don't multiply extra opacity onto the fill.
Wrapper padding 0/12/12/12: the sheet is inset 12 on each side and floats 12 above the bottom.
Use Sheet in apps, not SideSheet.

CardDialog.text: No title — all content (including the title) goes in the Slot; the header only holds a right-aligned close button.
Banner=True: a single 16:9 image; it is content, so it needs alt.
The close button over the image uses IconButtonNeutral Solid Small — an outlined button would disappear.
Dialogs don't stack — no back button.

Dialog.text: A screen template — in code build it from CardDialog and add the scrim yourself.
The panel is vertically centered (unlike Bottom sheet, which hugs the bottom).
Scrim overlay + overlay-blur 16, panel inset 12 on each side; don't multiply extra opacity onto the fill.
Confirm destructive actions with a Dialog containing a Solid TextButtonDanger.

SideSheet.text: A panel sliding in from the right edge of a desktop screen to view / edit details without leaving the page.
Standard sits beside the content with a left border, no scrim; Modal has elevation-high, two rounded left corners, a scrim like Sheet.
Footer: TextButtonNeutral Outline Base + TextButtonAccent Solid Base, right-aligned, gap 12.
Never use SideSheet in apps — use Sheet.
Width=Wide (480) for long / multi-column forms; default Base 384.
No left side sheet, no drag-to-resize.

Popover.text: A floating frame anchored to an element, holding interactive content (short forms, small confirmations).
Opens on press; closes with the close button / Esc / outside click.
Footer right-aligned, gap 8: TextButtonNeutral Ghost Small + TextButtonAccent Solid Small.
Don't use Popover for option lists (that is Menu) or hover explanations (that is Tooltip).
Anchored below the element, left-aligned; flips up when there is no room, right-aligns near the right edge.
No arrow — Popover separates by elevation.

ResultScreen.text: The task is done; the user has to go somewhere else.
The footer is a vertical ButtonGroup — primary on top, secondary path below.
Has a code component ResultScreen / UuResultScreen (Body + Footer; the screen places the NavigationBar); a square image with no background, needs alt.

ErrorScreen.text: An error blocking the whole core function that can't fix itself; a single-block error uses ErrorSection, errors fixable right away use Dialog / Toast.
Illustration in a 128 circle with background-accent-muted, needs alt.
Has a code component ErrorScreen / UuErrorScreen taking exactly one retry button.

EmptyScreen.text: The whole screen has no data yet.
One action button (create, explore), can be hidden with Action.
Has a back button (Back action=true) — an empty screen is still a normal screen.
Illustration in a 128 circle with background-accent-muted, needs alt.

EmptySection.text: A block inside a screen with no data yet (empty list, empty table), including inside a table body.
One button, can be hidden with Action.
Title heading-sm (smaller than the screen), centered; 128 round image with background-accent-muted, needs alt.

ErrorSection.text: The error is only in one block; the rest of the screen still works.
Title heading-sm centered; 128 round image with background-accent-muted, needs alt.
